instruction: `run(command, a, b)` in commands.py is a long if/elif chain. Refactor it to use a module-level dict named `OPERATIONS` that maps each command name ('add', 'sub', 'mul', 'div', 'pow', 'max', 'min') to a callable taking (a, b). `run` must look the command up in `OPERATIONS` at call time (so adding an entry to OPERATIONS makes it available to run) and must not contain any if/elif comparisons against command names. Behavior must not change: command names are matched case-insensitively after stripping surrounding whitespace, an unknown command raises ValueError whose message contains the original command string, and 'div' by zero still raises ZeroDivisionError. All tests in tests/test_commands.py must pass.
